text:
sam: Heads-up — product wants to start surfacing a console "compat mode" banner for v1 users before we flip any routing. question: what exact traffic/routing behavior should that banner imply?

anya: I think the banner should be purely informational initially — show expected sunset date, migration docs, and per-route impact estimates. No automated rerouting until we enable a soft-fallback in the service.

mike: Agree on info-only. We should define a clear mapping: if header X-Client-Version=v1 then route to legacy pool until grace-end. After soft-fallback window, do probe-based downgrade to v1-compat variant.

liz: Important: quotas. If we keep routing v1 traffic to legacy pools, those should be counted against the customer's v2 quota? or keep separate? Ops says separate quotas lead to complexity.

nav: Ops here — separate quotas explode billing and quota tooling. Proposal: treat incoming v1 requests as the same billing entity but tag telemetry with "client_version=v1" so we can slice. Quota enforcement remains on account+route.

sam: That tagging sounds good. For the banner UX we also need a projected latency delta and cost delta per route. Can we compute that?

mike: We can approximate. Two signals: kernel latency difference between pools + extra prefix cache misses. I can throw together a small estimator: 
```
estimate(route) {
  base_latency = median_latency(v2_pool, route)
  legacy_add = 10ms + cache_miss_penalty(route)
  return base_latency + legacy_add
}
```
Not perfect but gives product numbers.

anya: Telemetry needs: 1) client_version tag 2) route_affinity boolean 3) fallback_count 4) rollouts.sample_bucket. These let us alert on regressions.

liz: On deprecation timeline: legal wants a 90-day notice, but engineering wants a longer migration runway for large customers. Can we default to 120 days but allow per-customer exemptions?

nav: We can. Add a grace_exemptions list keyed by account id. Runtime will check exemption and skip reroute + skip quota delta. Audit logs must record exemption evaluation.

sam: How do we implement soft-fallback? two-phase: 1) dry-run probe: mirror a small % to v2 and compare outputs 2) flip a routing flag that will send >95% to v2 but keep a small fallback path to v1 when v2 errors/timeouts.

mike: Implementation detail: routing keys will be (account, route, client_version). We can add a runtime flag `compat_mode: OFF|DRYRUN|ENFORCE`. DRYRUN mirrors traffic to v2 but doesn't change response. ENFORCE uses v2 first, with fallback to v1 on error.

liz: On quotas during ENFORCE: we need to make sure customers don't get double-charged when mirroring. Mirror requests must be metered but not billed. Add `billing_action: mirror_no_charge` for mirrored probes.

anya: Console UX: banner + per-route migration panel. Panel shows % migrated, failed fallbacks, top failing prompt samples (anonymized), estimated cost delta, and a link to 'start migration' which flips compat_mode. Also surface a small toggle for account exemptions.

nav: Telemetry naming conventions: `redwood.client_version`, `redwood.compat_mode`, `redwood.fallback_reason`, `redwood.mirror_sample`. Please use these exact keys so downstream charts line up.

mike: Also add a debug header `X-Redwood-Compat: mirror/served-from-v2/fallback-v1` so customers can trace behavior in their logs. Example: 
```http
X-Client-Version: v1
X-Redwood-Compat: served-from-v2
```

sam: Good. One more: rollout alerts. If fallback-rate > 1% for 5m we should auto-pause ENFORCE and notify #oncall + the account owner.

deploy-bot: deploy log: compat-router v3 started canary at 2425002000, 5% traffic.

liz: Nice. For the migration docs please add recommended prompt hygiene checklist and a prompt-level diff tool sample. Customers often hit behavioral regressions not latency.

anya: For telemetry retention, keep compat tags for 180 days to analyze post-sunset trends. We'll need a retention exception for legal hold.

mike: Action items: 1) I'll add the runtime flags + debug header (PR today). 2) Nav will add telemetry keys + exemption checks. 3) Product (Sam/Anya) will prototype the console panel copy + estimated metrics. 4) Ops (Liz) will draft billing rules for mirror_no_charge and per-account exemptions.

sam: Thanks — let's meet briefly tomorrow to agree the exact console strings. If anyone objects to the ENFORCE behavior above speak up now. :thumbsup:

nav: +1 from infra.

mike: +1 will post link to PR when ready.

liz: +1 on billing plan, I'll ping finance for the exemption SKU.

anya: putting notes into migration doc.

deploy-bot: canary observed: fallback-rate=0.2% over last 5m, avg added latency ~12ms."
